tier_reason: Peer-reviewed ICS 2015 paper (arXiv 1503.05032) benchmarks CSR5 against MKL, cuSPARSE, CUSP, pOSKI, BiCSB, ViennaCL etc. and states the 17.6/28.5/173.0/293.3% average gains over the best existing method on 10 irregular matrices; compilers and CPU stated but flags not in the paper, and the repo's main.cpp runs only CSR5 (no baseline), so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: On 10 irregular matrices, average improvement over the best existing method per platform: 17.6% (dual Xeon CPU, best was pOSKI), 28.5% (GTX 980), 173.0% (R9 290X), 293.3% (Xeon Phi); up to 213.3%, 153.6%, 405.1%, 943.3%
corrections.caveats: ICS 2015 paper with 2015-era baselines; the 'best existing work' differs per platform (pOSKI on CPU, not MKL); paper gives no compiler flags (repo Makefile uses -O3 -mavx2 -march=native -fopenmp); repo benchmark runs CSR5 only; last commit 2020-12-26.

notes: Numbers match the abstract exactly. Repo MIT, 111 stars, not archived; last commit Dec 2020 so abandoned.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed IJHPCA 2024 paper reports Ginkgo mixed-precision AMG ~1.5x faster than AmgX (20-40% per-iteration), BatchBicgstab ~2x over MAGMA batched, and 1.8-2.4x ACOPF vs MA57 CPU baseline; no compiler flags, so not A.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Mixed-precision AMG ~1.5x faster than AmgX on one MFEM case (20-40% faster preconditioner application per iteration); BatchBicgstab ~2x over MAGMA batched dense; ~90% less solver time than LAPACK dgbsv in XGC; 1.8-2.4x faster ACOPF on MI250X vs MA57 CPU baseline

notes: Numbers confirmed on the SAGE page; the MA57 comparison is GPU vs CPU (hardware-confounded). Repo BSD-3-Clause, 612 stars, last commit 2026-09-30, active.

tier_reason: Peer-reviewed SC17 paper with GCC 5.4.0 -O3, i7-5820K, median of 5 runs, against Eigen and CHOLMOD; benchmark harness for the baselines not confirmed public, so B not A. Verdict is downgrade because the triangular-solve claim was overstated.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Triangular solve: average 1.49x over Eigen; Cholesky: average speedups over Eigen and CHOLMOD of 3.8x and 1.5x (abstract), up to 6.3x vs Eigen and 2.4x vs CHOLMOD
corrections.caveats: SC17 paper numbers on an i7-5820K with GCC 5.4 -O3; the paper does not link the repo; repo README shows a misleading Apache badge (copied from micromatch) but LICENSE.txt is MIT (Halide-derived); last commit 2023-07-12.

notes: Record claimed 3.8x over Eigen for triangular solve; the paper says 1.49x (the 3.8x/1.5x averages are the abstract's factorization numbers). License found in LICENSE.txt (MIT text), so copyable.
